subject: Capacity agreement flexibility & GPU-price sensitivity — proposed amendment
messages:
From: Timothy Ng <tim.ng@acme.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: 2027-01-19T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Revisiting reserved capacity tenor given GPU cost swings

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — the PoC latency numbers look promising. Before we lock the committed capacity in the SOW, procurement has asked us to push on a couple of flexibility items around tenor and pricing because the public GPU market has been unusually volatile.

Specifically, Acme is asking if Redwood would consider:
- A 9-month minimum reservation term instead of 12 months, with an automatic 90-day review for top-up or downsize;
- A GPU-cost-sensitive discount collar: if a GPU spot/market index moves >15% vs our baseline, a pre-agreed true-up (up or down) to discount tiers;
- A mechanism to reduce committed SKU counts by up to 20% on quarterly review (with a short notice window) if utilization is below forecast.

I realize these are non-standard. From our side, we want to strike a balance so we can commit to the capacity Acme needs today without being locked into outsized exposure if GPU prices spike. Can you outline whether Redwood can offer any contracting levers here (price-pass-through, tiered discounts, shorter tenor with renewal option, or hedging/credit protections)?

Attached: a one-page summary from Acme procurement (attachment: acme-request-summary.pdf).

Best,
Tim
Procurement Manager, Acme AI

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-01-19T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Revisiting reserved capacity tenor given GPU cost swings

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. Thread below. High level: they want flexibility on tenor and a pricing collar tied to market GPU prices. They are mid-market but moving to production fast; this is a strategic expansion for our hosted + dedicated mix.

Questions for pricing/finance:
- What pricing levers can we offer without creating open-ended downside risk? (tiered discounts, true-up windows, capped credits)
- Can we do a 9-month term with an automatic 90-day review and a one-time extension option to reach 12 months?
- Operationally, if we allow a quarterly right to downsize up to 20% of SKUs, what are the lead times and padding we need to keep SLOs?

Karthik — would you take the lead on drafting a customer-facing amendment (term sheet) with 1–2 options (conservative vs flexible)? Marcus — please flag any finance guardrails or approval thresholds. Laura — FYI for deal ops and legal redline path.

Irene
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-20T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Revisiting reserved capacity tenor given GPU cost swings

Thanks — quick draft of options below. I attached a clean term sheet and a sensitivity model (pricing-sensitivity-model.xlsx) with simple scenarios. Key assumptions: baseline GPU index = $X/token-equivalent (see sheet).

Option A — Conservative (preferred by finance):
- Term: 12 months committed
- Discount: fixed committed discount (e.g., 22%) on reserved SKUs
- True-up: quarterly utilization true-up only upwards (customer pays for shortfall) — no automatic downward resizing except at renewal
- GPU-price clause: Redwood reserves right to reprice if GPU market index rises >25% for two consecutive months

Option B — Compromise (sales-friendly):
- Term: 9 months initial, auto-review at 90 days with mutual option to extend to 12 months
- Discount: tiered discounts linked to committed volume (18% base, 22% at +25% commit)
- True-up: quarterly true-up both directions with cap: customer can downsize up to 20% once per quarter; cumulative downsizes limited to 40% over the term
- GPU-price collar: if GPU market index moves >15% vs baseline, trigger a temporary collar adjustment for next quarter; adjustment limited to +/- 6 percentage points and subject to a cap of $Y/kGPU-hour to protect Redwood

Option C — Flexible with hedging (requires higher approval):
- Term: 9 months
- Discount: lower baseline (16%) with a GPU-cost pass-through band (+/-10%); Redwood and customer agree to share variance 60/40 in favor of Redwood outside band;
- Financial safeguard: upfront buffer credit (prepaid credit) to cover worst-case 3-month spike; monthly reconciliation

Notes:
- See the sensitivity model for the breakeven points where discounts + pass-through could result in negative unit economics.
- If we go with Option B or C we should require legal sign-off and VP-level approval for the pass-through language.

Attachments: term-sheet_ACME_v2.pdf, pricing-sensitivity-model.xlsx

I'll incorporate Marcus' guardrails when I get them and then send a customer-facing amendment.

- Karthik
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-21T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Revisiting reserved capacity tenor given GPU cost swings

Appreciate the clear options. Finance's position:
1) We can accept Option B with the following guardrails: quarterly downsizes allowed but any cumulative reduction >25% over 12 months requires finance review and an additional fee to cover reallocation/repurchase costs.
2) Any pass-through / collar language that exposes Redwood to downside must include a prepaid contingency (we recommend 1 month equivalent capacity prepaid) and an explicit cap on Redwood liability (no more than the prepaid buffer without separate executive approval).
3) Approval thresholds: anything that deviates from fixed discount + no pass-through requires VP-Finance sign-off.

Operational note (Laura): if we permit quarterly downsizes, Infra needs a 21-day notice to re-catalog capacity and the ability to burst to maintain latency SLOs for customer traffic. That should be captured in the amendment.

I'll draft a one-paragraph finance guardrail to include in the term sheet.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Financial Planning & Analysis, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Tim Ng <tim.ng@acme.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-23T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed amendment: 90-day review + GPU-price collar (for signature)

Tim — thanks for the ask and for being pragmatic. Attached is the proposed amendment (term-sheet_ACME_v2.pdf) that maps to Option B with the finance guardrails Marcus requested. High-level summary:
- 9-month initial commitment with a mutual 90-day review and one-time option to extend to 12 months;
- Quarterly true-up in both directions; per-quarter downsizes allowed up to 20% with cumulative cap of 30% across the term;
- GPU-price collar: triggers at >15% move vs baseline; adjustment band capped at +/-6 percentage points; a prepaid buffer equal to 1 month of committed spend is required at contract signature to cover potential downside during spikes;
- Operational lead times: 21-day notice for downsizes; Redwood guarantees burst capacity to preserve latency SLOs subject to single-event burst limits.

Next steps:
1) Please review and confirm by EOD Friday if this tracks — we can then issue a DocuSign amendment link. (DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/abcdef-ACME-amend)
2) If Acme needs a different prepaid amount or change to the cumulative downsize cap, flag and we'll escalate to VP-Finance.

Attachments: term-sheet_ACME_v2.pdf (clean amendment), pricing-sensitivity-model.xlsx (for Acme review), amendment-docusign-link.txt

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
